content.text: In Zimbabwe, where financial isolation and currency collapse have left digital sellers struggling to collect payments from international buyers, CoreMerch offers a sovereign commerce infrastructure solution that removes geographic barriers and empowers creators with full control over their online stores, payment processing, and data ownership. This deployment guide outlines the step-by-step process of deploying a blockchain-based payment system using Cloudflare infrastructure and NOWPayments, ensuring a seamless and secure experience for Zimbabwean digital sellers. With CoreMerch's Edge Commerce Stack, creators can deploy a fully operational online store with automatic crypto payment processing, instant product delivery, and full data ownership in just 48 hours, at a cost of $197 per deployment. The solution is not a workaround, but a base-layer infrastructure that gives creators the freedom to sell their digital products globally without relying on Stripe or other platforms. By following this guide, you will learn how to set up a payment and delivery pipeline, process transactions, and scale your online store using CoreMerch's infrastructure-as-code approach.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

CoreMerch's infrastructure is designed to work independently of Stripe and other payment platforms, which often restrict access to creators in certain regions or countries. By leveraging Cloudflare Pages, Workers, and Supabase, creators can host their online stores and manage transactions using a blockchain-based payment system that is not subject to the same restrictions. With NOWPayments, creators can accept over 300 cryptocurrencies, including popular options like Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Litecoin, and benefit from a 0.5% fee and no buyer account requirements. This infrastructure is not just a workaround, but a robust and secure solution that gives creators full control over their online stores and payment processing.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before you deploy the Edge Commerce Stack, you will need to create a GitHub account, set up a Cloudflare account, and install the NOWPayments plugin on your online store. You will also need to configure your SPF, DKIM, and DMARC settings to ensure secure email delivery and prevent spam. Additionally, you will need to plan your product catalog, including the creation of digital products, pricing, and product descriptions. With these foundational elements in place, you will be ready to deploy the Edge Commerce Stack and start selling your digital products online.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you will need to integrate NOWPayments with your online store using Cloudflare Workers. This involves installing the NOWPayments plugin, configuring your payment settings, and creating a webhook to automate transaction processing. You will also need to set up a file delivery system using Cloudflare R2 or Google Drive to ensure secure and instant delivery of digital products to your customers. With these components in place, you will have a seamless and secure payment and delivery pipeline that meets the needs of your online store and customers.
The blockchain has no map of restricted countries — a wallet in Harare processes identically to one in Hamburg.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once you have set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you are ready to go live and process your first transaction. To do this, you will need to test your online store and payment system to ensure that everything is working as expected. You will also need to configure your payment settings, including setting up your NOWPayments account and configuring your payment methods. With your online store live and your payment system configured, you will be able to process your first transaction and start selling your digital products online.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Once your infrastructure is running smoothly, you will need to scale your online store to meet growing demand. To do this, you will need to plan for increased traffic and transaction volumes, and configure your infrastructure to handle the load. You will also need to consider implementing caching, load balancing, and other performance optimization techniques to ensure a seamless user experience. With the Edge Commerce Stack, you will have the flexibility to scale your online store as needed, without relying on third-party platforms or services.
How can creators in Africa sell digital products to international buyers?

The most practical path for creators in restricted countries starts with NOWPayments configured to receive USDT on Tron as the primary payment coin. USDT is a stable coin pegged to the US dollar — your revenue does not fluctuate with crypto market movements. Tron network fees are under $0.10, and settlement takes under 60 seconds. Once USDT arrives in your wallet, you convert to local currency through P2P exchanges — Binance P2P is available in most countries and supports naira, cedis, Kenyan shillings, and Pakistani rupees. Local exchanges like Patricia in Nigeria and similar platforms in other markets provide additional options. The conversion takes 20-30 minutes on average and costs 2-5% — significantly less than PayPal's international transfer fees. The sovereign stack provides the storefront, the automated delivery, and the order management. NOWPayments handles the payment verification. P2P handles the conversion. Together, this is a complete operational pipeline from digital product sale to local currency in your hands.
Creators in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Pakistan, and Zimbabwe are operating sovereign stores with this infrastructure right now.
